title: Solute, solvent and solution
examples: What is the difference between a solute and a solvent?
Where does sugar go when it dissolves?

explain.say: When you stir sugar into your tea, where does the sugar go? It seems to vanish! Look at the board. On the left you can see the sugar grains sitting in the water, before you stir.

Now see the right side. The water particles pulled the sugar particles away, one by one, and spread them out. This is dissolving. The sugar is still there, which is why your tea tastes sweet. How could you prove it is still in the cup?

Let us name the parts. See the first group lit up? The solid that dissolves is the solute, like sugar or salt. The liquid it dissolves in is the solvent, usually water. Can you guess what the mix is called?

Yes, a solution! Look at the third group: sweet tea, seawater and lemonade are all solutions. A solution looks clear, not cloudy, because the particles are too tiny to see. What do you think happens if you keep adding sugar?

Great thinking! After a while no more will dissolve, however long you stir, and the solution is saturated, which means full. Some things, like sand, never dissolve in water: they are insoluble. Wow: one litre of seawater holds about 35 grams of dissolved salt.

faq.a: Water particles surround the sugar particles and pull them away from the crystal. The sugar spreads out so finely that you cannot see it, but it is still there.
asks: Where does sugar go when it dissolves?

faq.q: What is the difference between a solute and a solvent?
faq.a: The solute is the substance that dissolves, like salt. The solvent is the liquid it dissolves in, like water. Together they make a solution.
A saturated solution holds as much solute as it can at that temperature. Any extra just sits at the bottom.

faq.q: Does sugar dissolve faster in hot water?
faq.a: Yes. Hot water particles move faster and hit the sugar more often, so it dissolves sooner. Stirring and using smaller grains help too.
asks: How can you make something dissolve faster?

faq.q: Is mass lost when something dissolves?
faq.a: No. If you dissolve 10 grams of salt in 100 grams of water, the solution weighs 110 grams. All the particles are still there.

facts: In a solution, the substance that dissolves is the solute and the liquid it dissolves in is the solvent.
Average ocean water contains about 35 grams of dissolved salts per kilogram.

quiz.say: In salty water, what is the solvent?
quiz.show: In salty water, what is the solvent?
quiz.why: The solvent is the liquid that does the dissolving: water.

wrong.0: Salt is the solute, the substance that dissolves.
wrong.1: Salty water is the solution, the mixture of both.

quiz.say: You dissolve 5 g of sugar in 200 g of water. What is the mass of the solution?
quiz.show: You dissolve 5 g of sugar in 200 g of water. What is the mass of the solution?
quiz.why: Mass is conserved: 200 plus 5 makes 205 grams.

wrong.0: Dissolving never makes the mix lighter than the water alone.
wrong.2: The sugar has not gone; its mass is still in the solution.
